title: Animating taichi diagrams
text: taichi (yin-yang) symbol cyclical, motion unusually -brand geom. Instead forcing third variable (e.g. week) onto x-axis shrinking every glyph, can turn animation frame. frame clean category x state grid large, readable taichi. vignette shows combine geom_taichi() gganimate. gganimate Suggested dependency; install install.packages("gganimate") already.
code: library(ggplot2) library(ggtaichi) library(gganimate)

title: Animating taichi diagrams
text: geom_taichi() returns pair layers separated ggnewscale::new_scale_fill(), fish keeps fill scale legend. gganimate works layer level — splits every layer’s data transition variable builds one frame per state. two fish layers ordinary ggplot2 layers, gganimate treats independently two fill scales continue apply frame--frame. short: ggnewscale layer stack composes cleanly gganimate, special wrapper needed. (just theory: every recipe rendered frame--frame gganimate 1.0.11, legends per-fish fills intact every frame.)

title: Animating taichi diagrams
text: Use transition_states() frame variable discrete (e.g. week number), transition_time() continuous time. drive underlying fish layers. bundled states_tg data perfect showcase: instead squeezing 31 weeks onto x-axis, keep category x state grid large glyphs let weeks play frames. fills continuous, tweenr interpolates values smoothly consecutive weeks.
code: p <- ggplot(states_tg, aes(x = category, y = state)) +   geom_taichi(yin = Twitter, yang = Google) +   theme_taichi() +   labs(title = "Week {closest_state}") +   transition_states(week, transition_length = 1, state_length = 1)  # Render to a GIF (requires the gifski package) # animate(p, renderer = gifski_renderer()) # anim_save("taichi.gif", p)

title: Animating taichi diagrams
text: Taichi symbols always drawn round (sized square units, like grid::circleGrob()), coord_fixed() keeps cells square , glyphs fill evenly. Match animation dimensions grid:
code: p_fixed <- ggplot(states_tg, aes(x = category, y = state)) +   geom_taichi(yin = Twitter, yang = Google) +   coord_fixed() +   theme_taichi() +   transition_states(week, transition_length = 1, state_length = 1)  # animate(p_fixed, width = 800, height = 600, fps = 10)

title: Animating taichi diagrams
text: angle argument (see ?geom_taichi) can rotate glyph. Mapping angle expression frame variable animating produces iconic “turning taichi” — eyes = TRUE eye rides around fish’s head: Note state_length = 1 transition_length = 0: frame state, rotation advances crisp steps (least one two lengths must positive, gganimate allocate frames). grow-reveal instead, keep positive transition_length add enter_grow() plot.
code: spin <- data.frame(   x = 1, y = 1, yin = 5, yang = 5,   frame = 1:36 )  p_spin <- ggplot(spin, aes(x, y)) +   geom_taichi(yin = yin, yang = yang, angle = frame * 10,               eyes = TRUE) +   coord_fixed() +   theme_taichi() +   transition_states(frame, transition_length = 0, state_length = 1)  # animate(p_spin, width = 300, height = 300, fps = 12)

title: Animating taichi diagrams
text: gganimate::anim_save() writes animation file. MP4 output use ffmpeg_renderer() (requires system ffmpeg); GIF use gifski_renderer() (requires gifski package). Aim 10–15 fps enough frames motion smooth; coord_fixed() keeps every glyph round rendered video.

what: 2.1 What kind of design is a taichi grid?
title: ggtaichi — Future Features
text: Gleicher et al. (2011), Visual comparison information visualization, gives vocabulary. Every comparison design assembled three building blocks: juxtaposition (side side), superposition (top ), explicit encoding (compute relationship show ). taichi grid superposition design — two sources occupy one mark one position, makes spatial patterns co-registered directly comparable. taxonomy also names superposition’s weakness precisely: supports “similar?” “larger ?” “much larger?” — requires explicit encoding. package currently offers explicit encoding , single clearest structural gap (→ §3).

what: 2.2 What does the glyph literature say a glyph should do?

Fuchs et al. (2017), Systematic Review Experimental Studies Data Glyphs (IEEE TVCG), synthesises 64 user studies, four findings bear directly package: simple star glyph without contours performs best across several criteria — simplicity wins. argument piling channels making existing ones excellent. Contours help shape-similarity judgements distract data-similarity judgements. ggtaichi draws outline (colour, linewidth); default colour = NA therefore right default value comparison, classic black taichi border stay opt-documented stylistic, analytic, choice. Colour comparisons need common axis; position/length comparisons require mental rotation across grid. genuinely favourable result colour-filled glyph grid: unlike star polyline glyphs, taichi’s two fills can compared cell cell without realigning axes. Performance drops significantly number glyphs increases — every scalability study found . dense-grid guidance nicety; reordering grid structure visible glance (→ §5) first-class feature, polish. title: ggtaichi — Future Features
text: Problem. Superposition answers “bigger?” “much?” (§2.1). reader looking 12 × 8 taichi grid can see yang dominates quantify , currently way ask. Features. Design notes. explicit_channel = "eye_size" elegant option eyes already exist data channel visually subordinate: fills carry two sources, eye size carries gap. big eye means big difference, reads “look ” — semantically apt. explicit_channel = "angle" accurate option (direction/angle rank 3 vs colour’s rank 6), rotation already exists. Encoding yin − yang tilt make difference readable precision fills can never reach. costs glyph’s upright orientation, belongs behind explicit choice — highest-accuracy option available. geom_taichi_diff() honest escape hatch: sometimes right chart “much bigger” diverging heatmap, package offers one next signature glyph trustworthy one insists glyph. what: 5. Theme C — Making the grid readable
title: ggtaichi — Future Features
text: Problem. Every scalability study Fuchs et al. found performance degrades glyph count rises (§2.2), package’s docs now admit dense grids hard. Three interventions available, one unusually powerful. Features. Design notes. Seriation highest-value idea document §3 §4. taichi grid alphabetically-ordered categories hides structure; reordering rows columns hierarchical clustering two value vectors makes blocks similar cells adjacent, precisely pattern-detection task glyph good (§2.3). matrix-reordering literature established heatmaps decades, transfers directly. also cheap: stats::hclust + factor releveling, new dependency. Offer standalone data verb (composable, testable) convenience argument. Binned fills cheapest accuracy win available. Reading continuous luminance ramp rank-6 task; matching swatch one five discrete bins far closer categorical lookup. ggplot2 already ships binned scales; package needs () make sure compose discrete/ continuous auto-detection added 0.2.0, (b) provide scale_taichi_* constructors ledger listed §4c, (c) recommend binning large grids docs. label_colour = "auto" needs real contrast logic, fixed colour: compute fill’s relative luminance choose black white per cell (farver makes trivial). hard-coded label colour invisible half diverging palette. Labels honest space: refuse (warning) cell count text fit, rather drawing overlapping mush. ggfittext CRAN automatic shrink--fit wanted. Deps none required (Suggests: ggfittext optional). Effort M (seriation), S (binned scale constructors), M (labels). Risk low.
code: # 1. seriation — reorder rows/columns so structure becomes visible taichi_seriate(data, x, y, yin, yang,                method = c("hclust", "pca", "mean", "difference", "none")) geom_taichi(..., seriate = "hclust")     # or reorder the factors yourself  # 2. binned fills — match to legend bins instead of interpolating luminance geom_taichi(..., yin_scale = scale_fill_fermenter(n.breaks = 5), ...) scale_taichi_yin_binned(...); scale_taichi_yang_binned(...)  # 3. on-glyph values, for small grids geom_taichi(..., label = c("none", "both", "yin", "yang", "difference"),             label_size = 2.5, label_colour = "auto")

what: 6. Theme D — Placement beyond the regular grid [ledger §6, deferred]
title: ggtaichi — Future Features
text: Problem. Ward’s taxonomy (§2.2) describes space placement strategies; ggtaichi implements one point . map case particular , ledger says, “compelling demo”. Features. Design notes. Follow glyph-maps method rather improvising. Wickham et al. (2012) solve exactly : embed glyph’s local coordinate system map space explicit width/height, glyph shape stays constant position comes geography. 0.2.0 renderer already resolves radius draw time physical panel, idea means hard part done. map demo obvious cross-package partner. countryatlas produces ISO-reconciled country geometry centroids; two-source country comparison (e.g. two data providers’ estimates indicator) taichi map compelling joint vignette, neither package needs depend — just documented recipes. Overlap real problem continuous placement, Ward’s post-processing distortions framework: jitter, repulsion, snapping coarse grid (last preserves readability best closest package already well). Default "grid_snap" message saying happened, never silently overplot. coord_sf needs system dependencies CI, gate (Suggests: sf), keep vignette eval-guarded, add tiny synthetic sf fixture tests. Deps Suggests: sf, optionally ggrepel. Effort M (map), M (scatter + collision), S (taichi_layout). Risk medium — CI system deps overlap semantics.
code: # map placement — one taichi per region, at its centroid geom_taichi(..., placement = "map")          # inside coord_sf() taichi_map(sf_data, yin, yang, size = 0.6)   # convenience wrapper  # continuous (data-driven) placement with overlap resolution geom_taichi(..., placement = "scatter", collision = c("none", "jitter",                                                       "repel", "grid_snap"))  # structure-driven placement taichi_layout(data, method = c("pca", "mds", "umap"), yin, yang) #> returns x/y positions from the data's own structure, for geom_taichi()

what: 7. Theme E — Palette pairing is a correctness problem
title: ggtaichi — Future Features
text: Problem, real one. default palettes grey ramp (gray100 → gray0) yin red ramp (#FED7D8 → #C20824) yang. two ramps span luminance range, equal values produce equal visual weight — one fish systematically appear dominate. design whose entire purpose comparing two sources fairly, palette pairing aesthetics; chart’s validity. shared_limits fixed numeric half problem 0.2.0; perceptual half untouched. Features. Design notes. colorspace right tool CRAN. Sequential HCL ramps shared luminance trajectory different hues exactly construction needed, colorspace also provides CVD simulation check function. farver handles per-colour luminance arithmetic. taichi_check_palette() runnable current defaults result documented honestly. grey-vs-red unbalanced, say help page, offer palette = "balanced", consider changing default next major version loud NEWS note. silently change — 0.2.0 already made “default look must change” commitment. shared_legend = TRUE deserves re-read light. paints fish yin_colors identical values read identical ink — perceptually correct answer directly comparable sources, arguably recommended strongly currently . cost two sources distinguished position within glyph (top bulb vs bottom bulb), worth stating explicitly. print_safe pair (works greyscale) matters journal figures, two-hue design collapses. Pair ggpattern texture fills (§8) belt--braces option. theme also answer ledger’s “audit current red/grey defaults accessibility” note — function instead manual check. Deps Suggests: colorspace; farver (already ggplot2 dependency). Effort M. Risk low technically; sensitive part whether change defaults.
code: taichi_palette_pair(n = 5, hues = c(250, 20), luminance = c(30, 90),                     chroma = 60) #> two ramps, distinct in hue, matched in luminance and chroma trajectory  taichi_check_palette(yin_colors, yang_colors) #> per-step luminance and chroma of each ramp, the max luminance mismatch, #> CVD simulations (deutan/protan/tritan), and a pass/fail verdict  geom_taichi(..., palette = c("balanced", "viridis_pair", "brewer_pair",                              "diverging", "print_safe")) scale_taichi_yin_viridis_c(); scale_taichi_yang_viridis_c(); ...   # §4c

title: ggtaichi — Future Features
text: Ordered perceptual evidence (§2.3), novelty. Design notes. split-ratio channel defensible ledger assumed. Area outranks colour Cleveland & McGill, moving S-curve encode proportion gives accurate reading third fill . Ship behind explicit split = argument, default , split_range clamped away degenerate slivers, document trade-plainly: gain accuracy lose iconic 50/50 silhouette. Non-negotiable constraint: two fish must still tile circle exactly — extend Monte-Carlo tiling test grid split values ships. radius easy one needs care neighbour collision (§6’s problem miniature) classic area-vs-diameter scaling error — scale area, .e. radius ∝ √value, say . eye legend probably resolved building custom guide. Mapped eye size low-precision channel construction; honest resolution document eyes annotation/attention channel rather measured one, point users need legend radius split instead. custom guide grob real work channel encourage precise reading . (Decision, foregone conclusion — see §15.) Patterns accessibility backstop. ggpattern composes polygon grobs; striped yin crosshatched yang survive greyscale printing total colour-blindness. Cost: pattern rendering slow device- dependent, gate warn large grids. Resist adding seventh eighth colour channel. Fuchs et al.’s “simple star glyph without contours performs best” warning: past point, channels reduce glyph’s legibility rather information. package’s channel budget spent accurate channels (area, angle, position) §3–§5’s readability work. Deps Suggests: ggpattern. Effort M (split, geometry tests), S (radius), S (patterns). Risk medium split — touches one piece package proof behind .

Real data arrives long unaggregated, every user’s first step group_by() + summarise() get right, duplicate cells currently handled geom rather explicit statistical choice. Features. Design notes. stat_taichi() makes aggregation visible plot spec, tidyverse-idiomatic less error-prone silent handling. also gives natural home fun.min/fun.max uncertainty (§10) later encoded. taichi_check() small function outsized value geom particular input: turns four separate confusing failure modes (duplicate cells, missing combinations, one-sided NAs, many cells) one readable report. also natural place warn “142 cells labels legible” (§5) “two ramps luminance-mismatched” (§7). Continue 0.2.0 practice erroring + time offending column name — fix BUG-3 right ergonomic. Deps none. Effort M. Risk low.
